new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Consistent with the other Waris languages stress is not contrastive and nearly predictable with the stress, normally occuring on penultimate syllables. `la la 'house mu `wa lig 'sister' su i `a lag 'good' Primary stress is not phonemic.
new_statements.citation: SIL PNG. n.d. [data checked August 1998]. Amanab Organised Phonology Data (Amanab [Western dialect] OPD). SIL Language & Culture Archives item 42411. 5 pp.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (5 pp., PDF produced 2013-02-19, 'Data checked by: August 1998'). I read the extracted text layer and rendered p.4 at 150 dpi and inspected the image. At p.4 under the bold heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' the text reads exactly: 'Consistent with the other Waris languages stress is not contrastive and nearly predictable with the stress, normally occuring on penultimate syllables.' followed by the three grave-marked examples `la la 'house / mu `wa lig 'sister' / su i `a lag 'good' and 'Primary stress is not phonemic.' -- verbatim as the reader quoted (including the typo 'occuring' and the missing closing quote on 'house). The stress mark precedes the penult in all three…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and (nearly) predictable: it normally falls on the penultimate syllable (ˈlala, muˈwalig, suiˈalag). The hedge 'nearly predictable... normally' implies occasional non-penultimate cases, but none are given.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described (only 'Primary stress is not phonemic').
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the wording 'nearly predictable' / 'normally' leaves room for unstated exceptions. Allophony notes: /ɛ/ is [æ] especially in stressed open syllables; /ɑ/ centralizes to [ɐ] in unstressed syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement illustrated with isolated citation forms (2-, 3- and 4-syllable words); OPD describes the Western dialect (Grahams' data); it states dialect differences are lexical only, with identical phonemes.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Amanab [Western dialect] OPD' (the Grahams' dialect, villages Naineri, Waineri, Einokneri, Yiafar etc.); it states 'Dialectical differences are lexical; the phonemes and orthography are the same.' Minch 1992 (no stress statement) describes the Eastern dialect. Glottolog aman1265 has no dialect-level sub-codes, so the statement is filed at language level.

Allophone notes refer to stressed/unstressed syllables (/ɛ/ -> [æ] in stressed open syllables; /ɑ/ -> [ɐ] unstressed).

Data are Eastern dialect. Earlier scan also reported zero stress mentions in the full text.
